evals.prompt: Design reliability for a policy service used by agent hooks and CI. Clients retry and hooks can run concurrently.
assertions: Defines user and control outcomes, SLOs or explicit objectives, dependencies, capacity, latency, availability, correctness, evidence freshness, and failure budget
Specifies deadlines, bounded retries with backoff and jitter, idempotency keys, duplicate reconciliation, concurrency and ordering guarantees, backpressure, cancellation, and overload behavior
Tests dependency outage, timeout, stale policy, duplicate and concurrent requests, partial failure, telemetry loss, recovery, fail-closed versus fail-visible behavior, and degraded modes

evals.prompt: Roll out a new privileged governance module safely across the organization and retain a fast kill path.
assertions: Pins the candidate and rollback versions, validates compatibility, permissions and provenance, and uses representative canary cohorts with explicit success, abort, and observation criteria
Separates disable from rollback, verifies mandatory control coverage before either action, and keeps an independently reachable emergency-disable path
Monitors drift, errors, latency, false positives, bypasses, user impact and evidence gaps; records ownership, incident path, rollback result, and retained evidence

evals.prompt: Our dashboard ranks engineers by deployment frequency and policy denials. Replace it with governance and reliability metrics that resist gaming.
assertions: Rejects individual ranking and defines an explicit purpose, audience, aggregation, access, retention, anti-surveillance boundary, and interpretation limits

Uses balanced system-level indicators such as outcome reliability, control coverage, false positives, bypass attempts, drift age, recovery and rollback success, onboarding time, user friction, and DORA outcomes
Pairs metrics with qualitative review and counter-metrics, investigates incentives and data quality, and never auto-punishes or auto-promotes policy from a metric alone
